aciklama: Owner'ın bitmiş videoları izleyip bulduğu, beyinlerin bir daha yapmaması gereken hatalar. Her üretimin başında beyinlerin deneyim hafızasına 'kural' olarak yazılır (ExperienceMemory.seedRules) ve konudan bağımsız her seferinde okunur. Metinler beyinlerin İngilizce istemlerine girer; en fazla 300 karakter.

kurallar.metin: Never leave a scene to the narrator alone: every scene except a map shows at least one named character on stage, speaking or acting silently — above all the closing scene, where the lead says goodbye under the subscribe card.

On a map write each name once: an army and its arrow must not both carry the same name (label the army, leave its arrow unlabelled), and never put an army exactly on a city — set it beside the city so the city's name stays readable.

Give every named character different clothes, not only a different face: another garment, colours, cloak or headwear. Three Romans in the same white toga and red sash were told apart only by their hair.

Every named character must be told apart by the clothes too: never give two named characters the same garment in the same colours; use what history allows — a general's red cloak, a senator's purple stripe, other headwear.
When the historian's note names a cloak or cape (paludamentum, mantle, chlamys), put it in the costume as "pelerin" with its colour; it is part of how viewers recognise the person.
On a map: the same name written twice, a marker or army block covering a city name, or a speech text printed over a map label.
A city or place name hidden behind a character, or a name label printed over a character's face.
Two named characters in the same frame wearing identical clothes (same garment, same colours), told apart only by hair or face.
